Here’s the full 12-week plan summary starting Monday, 2026-06-01, consolidating strength + hypertrophy training, intensified Phase 2, cardio, HIIT, plyometrics/power, nutrition, recovery, and Week 12 testing. Use as a week-by-week guide.

Schedule overview (standard week)
- Mon: Upper 1 + optional 20–30 min Zone 2
- Tue: Lower 1
- Wed: Plyometric/Power Day (25–40 min) + 30–40 min Zone 2 (optional)
- Thu: Upper 2 + optional 20–30 min Zone 2
- Fri: Lower 2
- Sat: Dedicated HIIT Day (replaces prior GPP)
- Sun: 30–45 min easy walk/cycle (recovery)

Global training guidelines
- Progression: RIR/RPE-based. Hit top of rep range at target RIR → add load next week (upper +1–2.5 kg; lower +2.5–5 kg). If RPE drifts high, reduce 2.5–5%.
- Rest: Main lifts 2–4 min; accessories 60–90 s.
- Tempo: Control eccentrics 2–3 s unless noted; pause work inserted as programmed.
- Warm-up each lift day: 3–5 min light cardio + dynamic mobility; 3–4 ramp sets to first main lift.
- Core: 2 focused moves per lift day.
- Autoregulate: If bar speed/quality drops >10% or pain appears, cut one back-off set and hold load.

Phase 1: Foundation Hypertrophy + Technique (Weeks 1–4)
- Focus: Groove patterns, build work capacity and muscle. Moderate loads, 6–12 reps, RIR 1–2.
- Cardio: 2–3 Zone 2 sessions (20–30 min). HIIT: intro protocols on Sat. Plyos: extensive/landing skill on Wed.

Week 1 (2026-06-01)
- Mon Upper 1: Bench 4x6–8 @ RIR2 (3-1-1), 1-arm DB Row 4x8–10, Incline DB 3x10–12, Lat Pulldown 3x10–12, Lateral Raise 3x12–15, Face Pull 3x12–15, Core: Pallof + Dead bug.
- Tue Lower 1: High-bar Squat 4x6–8 @ RIR2, RDL 4x8–10, Walking Lunge 3x10/leg, Leg Curl 3x10–12, Standing Calf 4x10–12, Core: Side plank + Rollout.
- Wed Plyo/Power: Pogo, skipping, lateral hops, MB chest/overhead toss, 3 x 20 m strides (contacts ~70–80). Optional 20–30 min Zone 2.
- Thu Upper 2: OHP 4x6–8, Chest-supported Row 4x8–10, Dips or DB decline 3x6–8, Pull-up/Assisted 3x6–8, Rear Delt Fly 3x12–15, Curl 3x10–12, Triceps Pressdown 3x10–12.
- Fri Lower 2: Deadlift 4x4–6 @ RIR2, Front or Goblet Squat 3x8–10, Hip Thrust 4x8–10, Back Extension 3x10–12, Seated Calf 4x12–15, Core: Hanging Raise + Farmer carry.
- Sat HIIT: 8–10 x 30s hard / 90s easy (bike/row). Warm up/cooldown included.
- Sun: 20–30 min easy walk.

Week 2
- Slight load increases as able; add one set to a weak-point accessory if recovery good.
- Plyo: step-off landings, pogos, skater bounds, MB scoop/press; strides 4 x 20–30 m (contacts ~80–90).
- HIIT: repeat W1 or 8–10 x 30s/90s; Zone 2 2–3x20–25 min.

Week 3
- Keep RIR 1–2; progress load. Swap one vertical pull to single-arm pulldown.
- Plyo: CM box jump 4x3, mini-hurdle hops, broad jump to stick, lateral bounds, MB throws; 3 x 30 m @ 85% (contacts ~80–95).
- HIIT: 8–10 x 45s hard / 75s easy.

Week 4
- Aim upper presses toward 4x8 @ RIR1–2; deads 4x4–6 top of range if clean.
- Plyo: seated box jump, taller mini-hurdles, skater bounds, rotational MB; 4 x 30 m @ 85–90% (contacts ~90–100).
- HIIT: 6–8 x 45s/75s; Zone 2 3x25–30 min.

Phase 2: Strength Emphasis + Hypertrophy (Weeks 5–8) — intensified
- Focus: Heavier top sets (RPE 8.5–9), more back-off volume on compounds, targeted hypertrophy density (myo-reps/rest-pause/lengthened partials). Keep technique pristine.
- Cardio: Keep Zone 2; HIIT progresses; taper in Week 8. Plyo intensity rises Weeks 5–7, then taper Week 8.

Week 5
- Mon Upper 1: Bench top 1x4 @ RPE 8.5–9; 4x4–5 @ 87–90%. DB Row 4x8 heavy, Incline DB 3x8–10 @ RIR1, Weighted Pull-up 4x5, Lateral Raise myo-reps, Face Pull 3x12–15, Core: Heavy chops + Copenhagen.
- Tue Lower 1: Squat top 1x3–4 @ RPE 8.5–9; 4x3–4 @ 88–90%. RDL 4x6, RFESS 3x8/leg, Leg Curl 3x8–10 + lengthened partials, Calf 4x10–12 (pause), Core: Ab wheel + heavy carries.
- Wed Plyo: Depth drops to stick, box jumps 5x3, hurdle hop series, lateral bound progressions, MB pass-to-sprint; 2 x 10 m falling starts (contacts ~85–95). Optional 20–30 min Zone 2.
- Thu Upper 2: OHP top 1x3–4 @ 8.5; 4x3–4 @ 87–90%. Barbell Row 4x6–8, Close-grip Bench 3x6–8, Pulldown 3x8–10 @ RIR1, Rear Delt myo-reps, Curl heavy + optional rest-pause, Triceps 3x8–10.
- Fri Lower 2: Deadlift top 1x3 @ 8.5–9; 4x2–3 @ 88–90%. Front Squat 3x5–6, Hip Thrust 4x6–8 (last set RIR0–1), Back Extension 3x10–12, Seated Calf 4x12–15, Core: Hanging raise + anti-rotation.
- Sat HIIT: 10–12 x 45s hard / 60–75s easy (7.5–9 min hard). Sun easy walk.

Week 6
- Add load if Week 5 met targets; maintain quality.
- Main lifts: same top/back-off scheme; reduce one back-off if bar speed drops >10%.
- Tue Lower: add Nordics/slider curls 3x5–6.
- Wed Plyo: Depth drops, broad jump 5x2, rebound pogos, single-leg lateral sticks, MB OHB; 3 x 20–30 m accels @ 90% (contacts ~80–90).
- HIIT: as W5; Zone 2 3x30 min on non-leg days.

Week 7 (highest stress)
- Mon: Bench top 1x3 @ RPE 9; 4x3 @ 90–92%; accessories slightly heavier/denser.
- Tue: Squat top 1x2–3 @ RPE 9; 4x2–3 @ 90–92%; RDL heavy 3x5–6; hamstrings/calves as written.
- Wed Plyo: Depth jump to box 4x2–3, moderate hurdle hops 4x3, box jump 3x3, continuous skaters 3x6/side, MB shotput 3x4/side; low total contacts (~70–80).
- Thu: OHP top 1x2–3 @ 9; 4x2–3 @ 90–92%; rows/close-grip/pulls heavy but tidy.
- Fri: Deadlift top 1x2 @ 9; 4x1–2 @ 90–92%; secondary work moderate.
- Sat HIIT: choose low total hard time (option A 8 x 20s all-out/100s easy OR option B 6–8 x 60s/90s), cap hard time ≤6 min. Consider swapping for Zone 2 if legs heavy.

Week 8 (fatigue management/taper)
- Keep intensity ~RPE 8–8.5; cut back-offs by 40–50%; 1–2 accessory sets only.
- Wed Plyo: very light (depth drop 3x3, box jump 3x2, pogos 3x15, MB 3x5; contacts ~50–60).
- HIIT: 6–8 x 30s/90s at submax OR skip. Zone 2 only.

Phase 3: Peak Strength + Specific Hypertrophy (Weeks 9–12)
- Focus: express strength with lower-rep top sets and specific back-offs; maintain muscle; manage fatigue for testing. Cardio steady, HIIT moderate early, tapers late. Plyo volume low, quality high.

- By Week 7 you’ll see the highest training stress; Week 8 reduces volume to set up Weeks 9–12 strength expression.

- After testing, take a light transition week (2–3 full-body sessions @ 60–70%, 3x3–5) before the next block.

Here’s a practical hypertrophy-focused nutrition plan to layer onto the 12-week program. It provides clear targets, meal templates, timing guidance, weekly adjustments, and simple tracking so you can individualize to your client.

Calorie and macro targets
- Calorie surplus: start +200–300 kcal/day above current maintenance.
  - If unknown maintenance, estimate: 33–36 kcal/kg bodyweight on training days, 30–33 kcal/kg on rest days. Adjust weekly (see below).
- Protein: 1.8–2.2 g/kg/day (anchor at 2.0 g/kg if unsure).
- Fat: 0.6–0.8 g/kg/day.
- Carbs: fill remaining calories; typically 3.5–5.5 g/kg/day (higher on training days).

Training vs rest day setup
- Training days: +50–100 g carbs vs rest days; keep protein stable; fats toward the lower end (0.6–0.7 g/kg) to prioritize carbs.
- Rest days: drop 40–80 g carbs; fats can sit mid–upper range (0.7–0.8 g/kg).

Meal frequency and timing
- 3–5 meals/day works well; distribute protein evenly (0.3–0.5 g/kg/meal).
- Pre-training (1–2 hours before):
  - 30–70 g carbs + 20–40 g protein, low fat/fiber to avoid GI distress.
- Post-training (within 2 hours):
  - 30–70 g carbs + 20–40 g protein; include fruit or fast-digesting carb if appetite low.
- Pre-sleep snack:
  - 25–40 g slow/complete protein (e.g., Greek yogurt, cottage cheese, casein) to support overnight MPS; add 10–20 g fat if it helps satiety.

Hydration and electrolytes
- Fluids: 30–40 ml/kg/day baseline; +500–750 ml around training.
- Sodium: 300–600 mg pre-training if sessions are sweaty or in heat.
- Carbs in-session: optional 20–30 g/hour if lifting >75–90 minutes or doing GPP intervals.

Evidence-based supplements (optional)
- Creatine monohydrate: 3–5 g/day, any time; no cycling needed.
- Caffeine: 2–3 mg/kg 45–60 min pre-training as desired.
- Omega-3 (EPA/DHA): 1–2 g/day if oily fish <2x/week.
- Vitamin D: per bloodwork if deficient.
- Protein powder: whey or plant blend to help hit protein targets.

Food quality and micronutrients
- Emphasize minimally processed foods: lean proteins, whole grains, potatoes, legumes, fruit/veg (≥5 servings/day), dairy or fortified alternatives, nuts/seeds, olive/avocado oils.
- Iron and B12: ensure adequate intake, especially if plant-forward. Pair iron-rich foods with vitamin C sources.

Weekly adjustment protocol
- Target bodyweight gain: 0.25–0.5% per week.
  - If gain <0.1%/week by end of Week 2, add +100–150 kcal/day (primarily carbs).
  - If gain >0.6–0.7%/week for 2 weeks or noticeable fat spillover, reduce −100–150 kcal/day.
- Performance check: if lifts stall for 2+ weeks and recovery is good, increase carbs +25–50 g/day.
- Appetite check: if appetite tanks, shift calories toward liquid options (milk, smoothies, carb powders) and add calorie-dense foods (oils, nut butters).

Macro templates by bodyweight (examples; adjust to client)
- At 55 kg (121 lb) training day:
  - Calories ~2000–2150; Protein 110 g (2.0 g/kg); Fat 35–40 g (0.65–0.75 g/kg); Carbs 275–310 g
- At 65 kg (143 lb) training day:
  - Calories ~2350–2550; Protein 130 g; Fat 40–50 g; Carbs 330–370 g
- At 75 kg (165 lb) training day:
  - Calories ~2650–2850; Protein 150 g; Fat 45–55 g; Carbs 375–425 g
- Rest days: reduce carbs by ~50 g and/or total calories by ~150–250 while keeping protein stable.

Simple meal builder (pick 1 from each column per meal)
- Protein (25–40 g): chicken breast/thigh, turkey, 90–95% lean beef, pork tenderloin, salmon/tuna, eggs + whites, Greek yogurt/skyr, cottage cheese, tofu/tempeh, seitan, whey/plant protein shake
- Carb (40–80 g): rice, pasta, quinoa, oats, potatoes/sweet potatoes, whole-grain bread/wraps, beans/lentils, fruit, low-fiber cereal pre/post-workout
- Veg/fruit: 1–2 fists per meal; go colorful
- Fat (10–20 g when needed): olive oil, avocado, nuts/seeds, tahini, nut butters, fattier fish, cheese

Two example training-day menus
- Option A (3 meals + snack, ~2400 kcal at ~65 kg):
  - Breakfast: Greek yogurt bowl with oats, banana, honey, chia; 2 eggs on toast
  - Pre-training: Whey shake + rice cakes with jam
  - Post-training lunch: Chicken burrito bowl (rice, black beans, peppers/onions, corn, salsa, avocado)
  - Dinner: Salmon, potatoes, asparagus; olive oil drizzle
  - Snack (pre-sleep): Cottage cheese with berries
- Option B (4 meals, lower fat preworkout):
  - Meal 1: Oatmeal with whey, blueberries; 1 tbsp peanut butter
  - Meal 2 (pre): Turkey sandwich on sourdough + apple
  - Meal 3 (post): Beef and rice stir-fry with veggies; pineapple
  - Meal 4: Tofu curry with jasmine rice; yogurt on the side

Around training (apply to program schedule)
- Morning training: larger carb/protein dinner + pre-sleep casein; light pre (banana + whey) and bigger post.
- Evening training: balanced breakfast/lunch; pre (30–60 g carbs + 25–35 g protein); normal dinner post.

Managing GI comfort
- Keep preworkout fat/fiber modest. Choose low-FODMAP carb sources if sensitive (white rice, rice cakes, ripe banana).

Alcohol

Compliance and tracking

- Weekly: adjust calories per bodyweight trend and performance; note appetite, sleep, cycle-related factors (on COC, no phasing required).

Deload week (Week 12) nutrition

Putting it into practice

Here’s a simple, compatible cardio plan to layer onto the 12-week strength + hypertrophy program for general health without compromising gains.

Goals
- Health markers: improve VO2max, resting HR, blood pressure, and recovery.
- Volume target: 90–150 minutes/week total aerobic work (mix Zone 2 + brief intervals).
- Intensity balance: ~80–90% easy Zone 2, ~10–20% higher-intensity intervals.
- Placement: avoid interfering with lower-body strength (separate from heavy leg days by ≥6–8 hours or put cardio after upper days).

Weekly structure (default alongside existing lifting split)
- Mon (Upper 1): 20–30 min Zone 2 after lifting or later in the day.
- Tue (Lower 1): Off cardio.
- Wed (Rest): 30–40 min Zone 2 + 10 min mobility.
- Thu (Upper 2): 20–30 min Zone 2 after lifting or later.
- Fri (Lower 2): Off cardio.
- Sat (Optional GPP): keep as-written or swap for intervals (see below).
- Sun: 30–45 min easy walk or cycle (recovery-focused).

Intensity guide
- Zone 2 (easy–moderate): conversational pace, RPE 4–6/10; 60–75% HRmax or 65–75% HRR if using a monitor.
- Intervals (hard but controlled): RPE 8–9/10 on work bouts; full conversational recovery between reps.

Modalities (rotate to manage joint stress)
- Low-impact first: incline treadmill walking, cycling, rowing, elliptical.
- Outdoor options: brisk walk/jog, easy run if experienced.
- Keep hard intervals off the treadmill if novice; bike/rower are joint-friendly.

12-week progression
- Weeks 1–2
  - Zone 2: 2–3 sessions x 20–25 min (Mon, Wed, Thu).
  - Optional Sat: 6–8 rounds 30s moderate/60s easy on rower or bike (keep it submaximal).
  - Sun: 20–30 min easy walk.
- Weeks 3–4
  - Zone 2: 3 sessions x 25–30 min (Mon, Wed, Thu).
  - Sat Intervals (optional): 6–8 x 45s hard / 75s easy, total hard time ≤6 min.
  - Sun: 30–40 min easy walk/cycle.
- Weeks 5–6
  - Zone 2: 3 sessions x 30 min.
  - Sat Intervals: 8–10 x 45s hard / 75s easy OR 5 x 2-min hard / 2-min easy (choose one).
  - Keep total weekly hard time ≤12–15 min.
- Week 7
  - Zone 2: 2–3 sessions x 30–35 min (slight bump).
  - Sat Intervals: 6–8 x 60s hard / 90s easy.
- Week 8 (fatigue management)
  - Zone 2: 2 sessions x 20–25 min only; no intervals.
  - Add extra mobility/walking as desired.
- Week 9
  - Zone 2: 3 sessions x 25–30 min.
  - Sat Intervals: 6–8 x 60s hard / 90s easy OR 4 x 3-min hard / 3-min easy (threshold-ish).
- Week 10
  - Zone 2: 3 sessions x 30–35 min.
  - Sat Intervals: 8–10 x 45s hard / 75s easy (reduce if legs feel heavy).
- Week 11 (strength peak)
  - Zone 2: 2 sessions x 20–25 min; keep it easy.
  - Optional: 4–6 x 30s moderate / 60s easy only if feeling fresh.
- Week 12 (deload/test)
  - Zone 2: 2–3 sessions x 20–25 min easy. No high-intensity intervals.

Integration tips
- Do cardio after upper days or on rest days; avoid before heavy lower sessions.
- If it must be same session as lower day: finish lifting first, then short 15–20 min Zone 2.
- Shoes and surfaces: prioritize low-impact modalities if shin/knee/hip soreness appears.

Progression and autoregulation
- If legs feel heavy or bar speed drops, cut the week’s intervals by 50% or swap for Zone 2.
- If RHR is up >5–7 bpm or HRV is down for 2+ days, drop one Zone 2 session that week.
- Weather/constraints: replace a session with a 6–10k step brisk walk.

Optional fitness checks (non-fatigue inducing)
- 12-min Cooper bike/row distance OR a 3-min step test every 4 weeks (Weeks 1, 5, 9) to track aerobic fitness trends. Keep submaximal; don’t chase PRs during peak weeks.

Warm-up and cooldown (each cardio session)
- 3–5 min gentle ramp-up, then settle into target intensity.
- 3–5 min easy cooldown + 5 min mobility (hips, calves, t-spine) to aid recovery.

This cardio plan keeps weekly aerobic volume within health-promoting ranges, supports recovery, and slots cleanly around the lifting program without compromising hypertrophy.

Here’s how to add a dedicated HIIT day that supports conditioning without compromising the strength + hypertrophy plan (including your higher-intensity Phase 2). We’ll use low-impact modalities, cap total hard time, and place it to minimize interference.

Placement and structure
- Default slot: Saturday (replaces or upgrades the optional GPP day).
- Separation: keep ≥24 hours before Monday’s Upper 1 and ≥36–48 hours from Friday’s Lower 2 when possible. If legs feel beat up, run the HIIT on a bike/rower and reduce volume that week.

Intensity targets
- Work intervals: RPE 8.5–9.5 (hard, powerful; you should want the interval to end).
- Recovery intervals: RPE 2–3, full conversational pace.
- Warm-up: 8–10 min progressive ramp (see below).
- Cooldown: 5–8 min easy + light mobility.

Modalities (choose one and stick with it for 3–4 weeks)
- Assault/air bike, spin bike, rower/erg, ski erg.
- Secondary options if joint-tolerant: hill sprints or curved treadmill sprints (only if experienced; cap volume lower).

12-week HIIT progression (integrated with your phases)
- Weeks 1–2 (intro)
  - Protocol: 8–10 x 30s hard / 90s easy
  - Hard time: 4–5 min; Session time: ~24–28 min plus warm-up/cooldown
- Weeks 3–4
  - Protocol: 8–10 x 45s hard / 75s easy
  - Hard time: 6–7.5 min
- Weeks 5–6 (Phase 2 overload begins)
  - Protocol: 10–12 x 45s hard / 60–75s easy
  - Hard time: 7.5–9 min
  - Note: choose bike/rower to spare joints; keep cadence/power consistent across reps
- Week 7 (highest lifting stress)
  - Protocol option A (power focus): 8 x 20s hard / 100s easy (true sprints; low total hard time)
  - Protocol option B (if legs fresh): 6–8 x 60s hard / 90s easy
  - Pick one; cap hard time at ≤6 min
- Week 8 (fatigue management)
  - Protocol: 6–8 x 30s hard / 90s easy OR skip entirely if heavy fatigue
  - Keep it submaximal (RPE 8–8.5), not all-out
- Week 9
  - Protocol: 8–10 x 60s hard / 90s easy
  - Hard time: 8–10 min
- Week 10
  - Protocol: 5–6 x 2 min hard / 2 min easy (threshold/VO2 blend)
  - Hard time: 10–12 min; reduce Thursday cardio to easy Zone 2 only
- Week 11 (strength peak)
  - Protocol: 6–8 x 30s hard / 90s easy OR 10 x 15s hard / 75s easy (keep legs snappy)
  - Hard time: 3–4 min
- Week 12 (deload/test)
  - Protocol: 6–8 x 30s moderate-hard (RPE 8) / 90s easy, or skip if testing maximals
  - Keep HR below near-max levels; prioritize recovery

Warm-up (8–10 min)
- 3 min easy spin/row.
- 3 min build to Zone 2–3.
- 3–4 x 10s pickups with 50–60s easy between (prime the system).

Cooldown (5–8 min)
- Easy spin/row until HR <60% HRmax.
- 5 min mobility: hip flexor stretch, hamstring floss, calf/ankle work.

Power/quality cues
- Aim for consistent power output across intervals; if using a bike/erg, hold watts within ±5–10% of the first hard rep.

- Keep total weekly hard interval time ≤12–15 min (HIIT day counts toward this).
- On weeks where legs feel heavy or bar speed drops:
  - Reduce HIIT reps by 30–50% or swap to 20–25 min Zone 2.
  - Avoid running-based HIIT; choose bike/rower.
- Post-HIIT fueling: 30–60 g carbs + 20–30 g protein within 1 hour to support next lift.

Optional session variants (rotate every 3–4 weeks if bored)
- Rower: 10 x 40s hard / 80s easy @ stroke rate 28–32, focus on drive power.
- Bike: 12 x 30s hard / 90s easy @ 100–120% FTP (if known) or target watts equal to the first rep’s peak minus 5–10%.
- Ski erg: 6–8 x 60s hard / 90s easy, emphasize tall posture and hip hinge.

Safety and readiness checks
- Skip or downshift HIIT if: sleep <6 h, DOMS 7/10 in quads/hams, RHR up >7 bpm from baseline, or persistent joint pain.

Here’s how to add a dedicated plyometric/power day that complements the 4-day Upper/Lower split, HIIT, and cardio without interfering with strength/hypertrophy. We’ll use low-to-moderate total contacts, prioritize quality and intent, and progress from extensive (landing skill, elasticity) to intensive (higher outputs). Default slot is Wednesday (the midweek rest day) or Saturday paired before easy Zone 2; avoid placing it within 24 hours before heavy lower sessions when possible.

Key principles
- Keep it short and snappy: 25–40 minutes total including warm-up.
- Do it fresh: schedule when not sore/fatigued; after a rest day or away from heavy lower days.
- Quality over quantity: crisp landings, tall posture, stiff ankles, minimal ground contact time.
- Contacts per session: start 60–80, progress to 80–110 by mid-block, taper to 40–60 before peak weeks.
- Surfaces: grass, turf, rubber track, or gym floor with good shoes.

Weekly placement options
- Preferred: Wednesday morning/afternoon (separate from lifting).
- If Saturday: do power first, then easy Zone 2 cardio later; keep HIIT on a different week or later in the day if legs feel fresh.
- Avoid the day before heavy squats/deads; if necessary, reduce lower-body emphasis that week.

Warm-up (10–12 min, every session)
- 3–5 min easy cycle/jog/row
- Dynamic mobility: ankle rocks, leg swings, walking hip openers, t-spine rotations
- Activation and primers:
  - A-skips 2x20 m
  - Ankling 2x20 m
  - High-knee runs 2x20 m
  - 2–3 accelerations 20 m @ 70–80% effort or 3 x 5 pogo jumps

Progression overview by phase
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): extensive plyos, landing mechanics, low amplitude, build stiffness/reactivity.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): elevate intensity and power—box jumps, bounds, med-ball throws; keep contacts controlled given higher lifting intensity.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): sharpen with low-volume, high-quality explosive work; taper volume in Weeks 11–12.

Week 1 (extensive)
- Pogo jumps (ankle pops): 3x20 contacts
- Skipping for height: 3x20 contacts
- Lateral line hops (two-feet): 3x15/side
- Med-ball chest pass (standing): 3x6 with quick reset
- Med-ball overhead toss (hip hinge start): 3x5
- Accel mechanics: 3 x 20 m fast strides (80%)
Contacts ~70–80

Week 2 (extensive + landing)
- Box step-off to stick (land mechanics) from 12–18 in: 3x5/side
- Pogo to stick (every 5th rep hold): 3x20
- Skater bounds (low amplitude) to stick: 3x6/side
- Med-ball scoop toss (rotational) 3x6/side
- Chest pass to rebounder or wall 3x6
- Fast strides: 4 x 20–30 m @ 80%
Contacts ~80–90

Week 3 (introduce small countermovement and horizontal work)
- Countermovement box jump (moderate box 16–24 in): 4x3, focus soft, quiet land
- Hurdle hops (mini hurdles, 4–6”): 4x5 continuous
- Broad jump to stick: 3x4
- Lateral bound (controlled) 3x6/side
- Med-ball overhead throw (tall kneeling) 3x5 + chest pass 3x5
- Accels: 3 x 30 m @ 85%
Contacts ~80–95

Week 4 (progress amplitude slightly)
- Seated box jump (reduces pre-load, teaches intent): 4x3
- Hurdle hops 5x4 (slightly taller)
- Continuous pogos 3x20 + 1x20 with last 5 reps higher
- Skater bounds 3x8/side
- Med-ball rotational scoop toss 3x6/side
- Accels: 4 x 30 m @ 85–90%
Contacts ~90–100

Week 5 (Phase 2 begins—intensity up, keep session tight)
- Depth drop to stick from 12–18 in: 3x4
- Box jump (countermovement) 5x3 (raise box if landings quiet and stacked)
- Hurdle hop series: 4x4 over 6–10” with fast ground contacts
- Lateral bound to mini-hop (bound then quick extra step) 3x6/side
- Med-ball chest pass to sprint: 3x3 passes + 10 m sprint
- Optional: 2 x 10 m falling starts (95% effort, not max)
Contacts ~85–95

Week 6 (power emphasis)
- Depth drop to stick 3x4 (increase height slightly if perfect)
- Broad jump 5x2 (full intent, stick each)
- Rebound pogo jumps (stiff ankles) 4x15
- Single-leg lateral bounds to stick 3x5/side
- Med-ball overhead back toss (MB OHB) 4x3 (outside or long space)
- 3 x 20–30 m accelerations @ 90%
Contacts ~80–90

Week 7 (highest intensity; trim volume slightly)
- Depth jump to box (step off 12–18 in, immediate jump to 20–24 in box): 4x2–3
- Hurdle hops 4x3 over moderate height with short ground contact
- Box jump (seated or regular) 3x3
- Skater bounds continuous 3x6/side (keep quality)
- Med-ball rotational shotput 3x4/side
- 2 x 20 m fly-ins (20 m build + 20 m fast), submax
Contacts ~70–80

Week 8 (taper—keep pop, reduce volume)
- Depth drop to stick 3x3
- Box jump 3x2
- Pogo jumps 3x15
- Med-ball chest pass 3x5
- 2 x 20 m accelerations @ 85–90%
Contacts ~50–60

Week 9 (sharpen—quality high, volume moderate)
- Depth drop to stick 3x3
- Box jump (choose best variation) 4x2–3
- Hurdle hops 3x3
- Broad jump 3x2
- Med-ball overhead 3x4
- 2–3 x 20–30 m accelerations @ 90%
Contacts ~60–70

Week 10 (power maintenance, keep intensity)
- Depth jump to box 4x2
- Rebound pogos 3x15
- Lateral bound to stick 3x4/side
- Med-ball rotational 3x4/side
- 2 x 30 m accelerations @ 90–92%
Contacts ~55–65

- Box jump 3x2 (moderate box, perfect land)
- Pogo jumps 3x12
- Med-ball chest pass 2x4
- 2 x 20 m accelerations @ 85–90%
Contacts ~35–45

- If testing heavy singles: skip power session.
- If not testing: keep to 2–3 crisp sets only:
  - Box jump 2x2, Pogos 2x10, Chest pass 2x4

Coaching cues
- Land “quiet and tall”: ribs down, hips back, knees track toes, absorb through hips.
- Ankles: think “stiff spring” on pogos/hops; minimize knee collapse.
- Horizontal jumps: full hip extension, stick land with shin angle neutral.
- Med-ball: brace, transfer force from legs/hips; no excessive lumbar extension.

- If doing HIIT on Saturday:
  - Make plyo day Wednesday.
  - If you must pair on Saturday: do plyos first (25–30 min), wait 4–6 hours, then HIIT; or replace HIIT that week with Zone 2.

- Use stable trainers with good forefoot; avoid heavy lifters. Choose forgiving surfaces (turf/track/wood floor).

Readiness and autoregulation
- Skip or cut volume 30–50% if: DOMS ≥7/10 in quads/hams, ankle/knee/hip joint discomfort, or poor sleep.
- End a drill if ground contact times slow or landings get noisy—quality ends the set.

Optional metrics
- Track best box height cleared with perfect land, standing broad jump distance, and med-ball throw distance monthly (Weeks 1, 5, 9). Don’t max—stop at the best clean rep.

Here’s a clear, low-risk 1RM testing plan for the end of Phase 3 to gauge progress. It fits your Week 12 deload, prioritizes accuracy and safety, and gives contingency options. You can test all four competition lifts (Squat, Bench, Deadlift, and optionally OHP) across three sessions.

Testing week structure (Week 12)
- Mon: Squat + Bench 1RM test
- Wed: Deadlift 1RM test + optional light OHP e1RM
- Fri: Optional OHP 1RM test (if you didn’t estimate it Wednesday) or repeat a lift if Monday/Wed was off
- Sat/Sun: Rest

General rules
- Arrive well-rested and fueled (normal carbs the day before and day of).
- Standardize equipment, stance, footwear, depth/range, and commands.
- Use a spotter for bench and safety pins/straps where available.
- Bar speed device is useful; if not, use RPE. Stop tests if technique breaks down.

Warm-up protocol (per lift)
- 5–7 min general warm-up (bike/row/walk) + dynamic mobility for hips/shoulders/ankles + 2–3 activation drills (band pull-aparts, glute bridges).
- Movement prep: Empty bar x 10–15 reps (2 sets).
- Ramped sets (approximate percentages based on last known e1RM or best single):
  - 5 reps @ 40–50%
  - 3 reps @ 60%
  - 2 reps @ 70%
  - 1 rep @ 80%
  - 1 rep @ 85–88%
  - 1 rep @ 90–92% (should feel fast and confident)
  - Then take singles as outlined below.
- Rest 2–3 min on warm-ups, 3–5+ min between heavy singles.

Attempt selection (percent- and RPE-based)
Use recent Week 11 top singles (RPE 8) to anchor attempts. If you don’t have a reliable e1RM, use the ranges below and autoregulate with bar speed/RPE.

Squat and Bench (Monday)
- Attempt 1 (Opener): 88–92% e1RM, target RPE 6–7. Should be a guaranteed rep that settles nerves.
- Attempt 2: 94–97% e1RM, target RPE 8–8.5. If it moves well, proceed to Attempt 3 for PR.
- Attempt 3 (PR attempt): 100–103% of current e1RM or +2.5–5 kg over previous best. If Attempt 2 was grindy (RPE 9.5), take a smaller jump or repeat for a cleaner 1RM.
- Optional 4th attempt (only if Attempt 3 was smooth ≤RPE 9): small PR (+1–2.5 kg upper, +2.5–5 kg lower).

Deadlift (Wednesday)
- Attempt 1: 90–92% e1RM (RPE 6–7).
- Attempt 2: 95–98% (RPE 8–8.5).
- Attempt 3: 100–104% or +2.5–7.5 kg PR attempt.
- Deadlift jumps can be larger; stay conservative if grip or back feels off.

Overhead Press (optional)
- If testing Monday/Wednesday already felt taxing, do OHP Friday; otherwise, take a heavy single @ RPE 8–9 on Wednesday after deadlifts and calculate e1RM.
- Attempt structure matches bench but with smaller jumps (1–2.5 kg).

Bar speed and RPE checkpoints (help choose next attempt)
- Squat: if the last warm-up @ ~90% is ≥0.30 m/s or feels ≤RPE 7, green light for planned jumps. If <0.25 m/s or RPE ≥8, trim next jump by 2.5–5 kg.
- Bench: last warm-up ≥0.20–0.25 m/s or ≤RPE 7.5 to proceed as planned; slower = smaller jumps.
- Deadlift: last warm-up ≥0.25–0.30 m/s or ≤RPE 7.5; if slower, take conservative jumps.

Fail-safe rules
- One miss ends that lift’s testing; drop to a smooth back-off single @ ~90% and move on.
- Technique violation (depth, soft lockout) doesn’t count—either repeat with a smaller load or accept the best clean lift as the day’s 1RM.

Post-attempt back-offs (optional, only if you didn’t hit a maximal grinder)
- 1–2 x 1–2 at 85–90% for practice speed, only if you feel fresh and the top single was ≤RPE 9.

Recovery and fueling around tests
- Day before: normal calories with higher carbs; hydrate well, sodium-normal.
- Day of: pre-test meal 1–3 h prior with 30–80 g carbs + 20–40 g protein; caffeine 2–3 mg/kg if tolerated.
- Between lifts (Mon): 15–30 g quick carbs + fluids after squat before bench.
- Post-session: 30–60 g carbs + 25–40 g protein, normal dinner; sleep 8+ h.

Data capture
- Record: load, RPE, bar speed (if used), video for depth/form, bodyweight.
- Note: warm-up feel, any pain, footwear, belt settings, stance/grip widths.
- Calculate e1RMs using the best smooth single at RPE 9 or using bar speed tables if you have them.

Contingencies and modifications
- If fatigue is high in Week 12:
  - Convert to submax testing: work to a single @ RPE 8–8.5 and use e1RM (e.g., Epley or RIR-based charts). This is often within 92–96% of true 1RM.
- If time-limited:
  - Test one lift per day across Mon/Tue/Thu; skip optional OHP.
- If joints cranky:
  - Swap to close variants for assessment (e.g., trap bar deadlift 1RM, safety bar squat 1RM, long pause bench e1RM) and compare to prior baselines.

Example attempt cards (adjust to your client’s numbers)
- Squat e1RM 140 kg → Opener 125 kg (89%), Second 132.5 kg (95%), Third 140–145 kg.
- Bench e1RM 80 kg → Opener 72.5 kg (91%), Second 76 kg (95%), Third 80–82.5 kg.
- Deadlift e1RM 165 kg → Opener 150 kg (91%), Second 157.5–160 kg (95–97%), Third 165–172.5 kg.

After-action review and next block setup
- Compare best clean 1RMs and e1RMs to Week 1 baselines; expect the best singles to align with or exceed Week 11 @8 singles by ~5–10%.
- Identify weak links: sticking points, bar path, setup consistency; use this to select accessories next block.
- Schedule a light week after testing (2–3 full-body sessions @ ~60–70% for 3x3–5) before starting the next training cycle.

This plan gives you a reliable, athlete-friendly 1RM assessment that slots into your deload week, captures meaningful progress, and preserves momentum for the next block.
